_about: Radio tower: the strike's one ground target (Alex's decision strike-target, 2026-10-10: 'A radio tower'). A STATIC unit (mobility 'static'): it never moves, turns or plans, has no weapons, and goes down with the fate 'destroyed' when its health reaches 0 -- from bombs (scripts/sim/bombs.gd; guns could, in principle, if a cone ever reached the ground). Its band is the surface. EVERY NUMBER IS PROPOSED by Track S2 (2026-10-10) for the strike; the numbers behind the proposals are in the tuning table in the report. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Radio tower

size_m._reason: the footprint of a lattice mast and its guy-wire anchors seen from above; the tower itself is thin, so the plan view is mostly its shadow

draught_m._reason: a unit that does not float needs no water under it (the water rule, World.set_water, applies to domain sea only): 0

actions_per_turn._reason: a static unit has nothing to plan: one step a turn that stands still (the World gives it a two-state history, start and end, both the same)

health._reason: pips the bombs must take (3 for a hit within 12 m, 2 within 25 m, 1 within 45 m: data/sim/bombs.json). 8 pips is three direct hits, or a dozen near misses. A bomber's stick of four at the ideal release angle does 7.9 pips on average from the low band (the tower dies to the first stick 62 percent of the time, 1.4 drops on average), 4.8 from medium (2.2 drops; dead within the bomber's three drops 98 percent of the time) and 1.8 from high (5.3 drops; 19 percent): the tuning table, scripts/test_support/strike_tuning.gd B

sight_range_m._reason: a tower with a lookout on it sees a fighter a few hundred metres out; the enemy AI counts what its units see (scripts/sim/ai_sense.gd), so this is how far the tower warns the patrol

material._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (2026-10-12; the board's table, variants/gunfire/board.json material_table, which Alex's decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', and gunfire-looks, G3, put to use): a lattice mast (the effects draw its ruin as a falling steel mast). Decides what a round that lands on it does (data/fx/fx.json gunfire): metal.

enabled._reason: the equipment at the foot of the mast burns when the tower is hit

source_m._reason: the hut and the equipment at the foot of the mast, not the 12 m footprint (the mast itself is a thin line)

source_back_m._reason: the foot of the mast is the unit's centre

rise_mps._reason: the smoulder's rate: a damaged ground or sea unit smokes like a ruin or a wreck (data/fx/fx.json ruin R1 and crash A smolder rise_mps 4.0), so its puffs climb into the faster air above and the plume leans downwind (decisions smoke-consistency, wind-with-height). PROPOSED

shape._about: One box: the lattice mast. The art's tower is 23-27 m (docs/proposals/shot-heights.md); a thin lattice, so the box is narrow. Not stamped (it is a target, not cover). Every number PROPOSED.

stamp._reason: a target, not scenery: other lines are not blocked by it

length_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 3.0 m, a mast's base seen from above (size_m 12 is the guy anchors' footprint)

width_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 3.0 m, square

bottom_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): on the ground

top_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 25 m, the middle of the art's 23-27 m. Material armour stands for 'metal': the damage-looks table has no steel row

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: static: never turns (the exponent is unused; it must be a number)

altitude_bands._reason: it stands on the ground: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json)
